LAYER 1 WIRE LATH Self-furring metal lath nailed at 6" centers LAYER 2 WESTERN ONE-COAT 3/4 inch base coat 6–7 day water cure LAYER 3 SENERGY COLOR COAT Elastomeric finish 150+ SW colors MODERN TWO-COAT SYSTEM Western One-Coat + Senergy Color Double-ply building paper — two layers Grade D moisture barrier. Lapped correctly. Every window, door, and penetration flashed before lath. Wire lath — self-furring metal lath nailed to studs at 6-inch centers. Correct overlap, corner bead and control joints at all structural transitions. Western One-Coat 3/4 inch base — applied in one monolithic coat. Dense, hard. The modern standard for Utah homes. Superior to multi-step scratch/brown systems. 6 to 7 day water cure — maximum water applied every day. Walls crack out in controlled hairlines. After cure, walls are as hard as they will ever get. Senergy color coat — 100% acrylic elastomeric finish. 150+ Sherwin-Williams colors. 300% more elastic than paint. Applied after full cure. Best for — all Utah residential and commercial new construction and remodel. Dallas's standard system on every job today. EIFS SYSTEM Exterior Insulation & Finish System Drainage plane — always — Dallas never installs barrier EIFS. A proper drainage plane is non-negotiable. He has fixed hundreds of failed barrier EIFS jobs. Atlas EnergyShield foam board — continuous R-value. No thermal bridging. The insulation layer that makes EIFS the most energy-efficient exterior available. Senergy Alpha base coat with full mesh — fiberglass mesh fully embedded at full thickness. Never short-coated. Full strength always. Senergy Conflex XL finish — elastomeric color coat. 150+ SW colors. 300% more elastic than paint. Exceptional long-term weather performance. Best for — energy efficiency upgrades, existing EIFS replacement, wood-frame homes in climate-sensitive Utah microclimates. Dallas's honest note — EIFS done wrong causes massive moisture damage. Dallas has the forensic experience to install it right and fix it when others don't. 6–7 DAYS WHY DALLAS FLOODS THE WALLS WITH AS MUCH WATER AS POSSIBLE Portland cement and Western One-Coat gain strength through hydration — a chemical reaction that requires water. If the base coat dries too fast it does not fully hydrate. The walls are weaker. Cracks are random and large. Dallas floods the walls with as much water as possible every day for 6 to 7 days. The walls crack out in controlled hairlines during this phase — that is correct and expected. After the Senergy color coat goes on, the walls are as hard as they will ever get. Dallas tells every customer this before the job starts. No surprises. 01 SUBSTRATE INSPECTION Full inspection of sheathing and moisture barrier. Any damage found and documented on video before work begins. 02 DOUBLE-PLY BARRIER Two layers Grade D paper. BROWSE ALL SW COLORS → GET A FREE ESTIMATE STUCCO FAQ — ANSWERED HONESTLY STUCCO QUESTIONS. STRAIGHT ANSWERS. How much does stucco installation cost in Utah? New stucco installation in Utah typically runs $8 to $14 per square foot installed. A 2,000 square foot home runs $16,000 to $28,000 depending on substrate condition, complexity, and system chosen. Dallas provides a written itemized estimate — call (801) 518-5030. Will my new stucco crack? Hairline shrinkage cracks are a normal characteristic of Portland cement stucco — not a defect. Dallas floods the walls with as much water as possible for 6 to 7 days during cure. This controls the cracking so it appears as fine hairlines during cure rather than random cracks later. Dallas tells every customer this before starting. No surprises. What is the difference between the two-coat system and EIFS? Dallas's modern two-coat system (double-ply paper + wire lath + Western One-Coat 3/4 inch base + Senergy color coat) is his standard for Utah homes — more impact resistant and better for masonry substrates. EIFS provides superior insulation and is better for wood-frame homes needing energy efficiency. Dallas assesses your specific home and recommends the right system — not just the one he prefers to install. How long does stucco installation take? A typical single family home takes 2 to 3 weeks including the 6 to 7 day water cure period. Complex homes with multiple gables and roofline transitions take longer. Dallas provides a detailed schedule with every written estimate. What warranty comes with new stucco installation? Christensen Stucco provides honest scoped warranties: 2-year workmanship on new stucco installation, 1-year on stucco repairs, 5-year on water damage moisture barrier and flashing rebuilds, and 2-year labor on Hardie, Trex, and window installations (plus full manufacturer warranties on those products). UV fade, normal weathering, and other contractors' work are excluded. Every warranty is in writing before work starts. Dallas explains all of this before any contract is signed. Stucco-to-Hardie conversions cost more due to the removal scope. Dallas provides a written itemized estimate — call (801) 518-5030. Can Hardie go over existing stucco? In some cases technically yes — but Dallas does not recommend it. Installing over stucco prevents proper sheathing inspection, limits moisture barrier replacement, creates fastening issues, and the result is not eligible for the full 30-year warranty. Full removal produces a better installation, a better warranty, and eliminates the risk of covering hidden moisture damage. How long does Hardie installation take? A standard Hardie installation takes 1 to 2 weeks. A stucco-to-Hardie conversion takes 2 to 4 weeks due to the removal and sheathing inspection scope. The reason most window contractors leave visible patches in stucco is they don't understand the stucco system they're cutting into. Dallas is a 40-year stucco master who installs windows. That combination doesn't exist anywhere else in Utah. The 6-Inch Rule When opening stucco for a window Dallas never exceeds 6 inches beyond the rough opening. Beyond 6 inches the patch becomes visible no matter how well it's color matched. Every opening is scored, cut, and closed with surgical precision. The patch disappears into the wall. What Happens When Contractors Get It Wrong Stucco cut too wide. Felt paper torn. No flashing. Foam backer rod stuffed in the gap. Patch painted over. Within one Utah winter — freeze-thaw drives water through that gap. The sheathing starts rotting. Dallas has rebuilt hundreds of failed window installations. He does not create them. Get a Window Estimate → The Correct 6-Step Process 1 Score the perimeter Grinder with diamond blade scores the stucco at the exact opening size. Clean cut. No cracking into adjacent wall. 2 Remove stucco — expose felt paper Stucco chiseled carefully back to the felt paper. The felt paper must not be torn — it is the moisture barrier. 3 Fold back felt paper intact Felt paper folded back without tearing. This is the most critical step. A torn felt paper means moisture gets behind the wall system. 4 Install window with full flashing Self-adhesive flashing tape at sill. Window set and shimmed. Head flashing installed. All penetrations sealed. No shortcuts. 5 Re-integrate felt paper Felt paper lapped correctly over the flashing. Moisture path directed away from the wall — not into it. 6 Close with color-matched stucco Multi-layer stucco patch applied. Texture matched. Color custom-blended to match existing weathered stucco. Invisible when done correctly. Window Styles Available Every style. One installer. Dallas installs every window style in every brand he carries. Window replacement in a stucco home runs $800 to $2,500 per window installed including the stucco repair around each opening. The stucco work adds cost compared to a siding home but is critical to moisture protection. Dallas provides a written itemized estimate — call (801) 518-5030. Will I see a patch around my new windows? Not if Dallas does the work. His 6-inch rule limits the opening to what can be closed invisibly. He custom blends the Senergy finish coat to match your existing weathered stucco — not just the original color formula. The patch becomes invisible. Contractors who leave visible patches exceeded the 6-inch rule or did not color match correctly. Can I get new windows without replacing all my stucco? Yes — window replacement is completely independent of stucco resurfacing. Dallas installs new windows in existing stucco, closes each opening invisibly, and color matches to the existing wall. If you want to resurface the entire house at the same time that is available as a combined project under one contract. How long does window replacement take in a stucco home? A typical full house window replacement on a stucco home takes 3 to 5 days for the installation plus 2 to 3 days for the stucco work around each opening to cure properly. Dallas does not rush the stucco cure. Total project typically 1 to 2 weeks depending on number of windows and home size. What warranty comes with window installation? Two warranties apply. The window manufacturer warranty — Milgard's Full Lifetime Warranty, Pella's limited warranty, or equivalent depending on brand chosen. Plus Dallas's 1-year workmanship warranty on the stucco integration, flashing, and installation work he performs. Both warranties are provided in writing before work starts.
